svg.font-family: 'Geist Mono', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

metadata.orrery:spec: # yaml-language-server: $schema=../references/diagram.schema.json # After Google's Cloud Architecture Center "Architecture for MLOps using TensorFlow Extended, # Agent Platform Pipelines, and Cloud Build": CI/CD with Cloud Build, triggers through Pub/Sub # and Cloud Run functions, a pipeline that runs its steps on Dataflow and Managed Training, # and Model Monitoring alerts that start the next run. title: MLOps on Google Cloud with Agent Platform subtitle: Cloud Build ships the pipeline; Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI) trains, registers and serves the model, and drift alerts retrain it direction: down # Product cards, as in Google Cloud's own architecture diagrams. look: card # The figure is one loop: delivery and triggers on top, the pipeline across the middle, # serving back along the bottom, and drift alerts up the left side to the triggers. layout: { spacing: compact } legend: solid: Delivery, training and inference dashed: Pipeline triggers dotted: Artifacts and lineage groups: source: { type: gcp:external, label: GitHub } gcloud: { type: gcp:cloud } project: { type: gcp:project, label: Project ml-prod, in: gcloud } pipeline: { type: gcp:tier, label: Agent Platform Pipelines, in: project } serving: { type: gcp:tier, label: Serving, in: project } # Agent Platform services (formerly Vertex AI) draw the Vertex AI core icon from Google's # product icon download. Cloud Run functions keeps the Serverless Computing icon that the # icon guide assigns to it under its former name, Cloud Functions. nodes: scientists: { icon: generic:users, label: Data scientists } repo: { icon: logos:github-icon, label: Source repository, note: Pipeline and component code, in: source } # The alert source first, above the left side where the drift alerts climb. logging: { icon: gcp:cloud-logging, label: Cloud Logging, note: Alert log filter, in: project } scheduler: { icon: gcp:cloud-scheduler, label: Cloud Scheduler, in: project } build: { icon: gcp:cloud-build, label: Cloud Build, note: Test and compile, in: project } topic: { icon: gcp:pubsub, label: Pub/Sub, note: Trigger topic, in: project } registry: { icon: gcp:artifact-registry, label: Artifact Registry, note: Images and pipeline template, in: project } # The training inputs share the launcher's row (align), right above the step that reads them. bigquery: { icon: gcp:bigquery, label: BigQuery, note: Training data, in: project, align: launcher } features: { icon: gcp:vertex-ai, label: Feature Store, in: project, align: launcher } launcher: { icon: gcp:cloud-functions, label: Cloud Run functions, note: Submits PipelineJob, in: project } # The steps run left to right in one row (align). prep: { icon: gcp:dataflow, label: Validate and transform, note: Dataflow, in: pipeline } train: { icon: gcp:vertex-ai, label: Managed Training, note: Train and tune, in: pipeline, align: prep } evaluate: { icon: gcp:dataflow, label: Evaluate and validate, note: Dataflow, in: pipeline, align: prep } artifacts: { icon: gcp:cloud-storage, label: Cloud Storage, note: Pipeline artifacts, in: project } metadata: { icon: gcp:vertex-ai, label: Vertex ML Metadata, note: Lineage, in: project } # Model Registry stores the model under the last step; serving runs back right to left in one # row (align), so Model Monitoring ends under Cloud Logging. models: { icon: gcp:vertex-ai, label: Model Registry, in: project } monitor: { icon: gcp:vertex-ai, label: Model Monitoring, note: Skew and drift, in: serving, align: endpoint } endpoint: { icon: gcp:vertex-ai, label: Endpoint, note: Online inference, in: serving } edges: - scientists -> repo: push - repo -> build: build trigger - build -> registry: push - registry -> launcher: pipeline template - scheduler, logging --> topic: publish - topic --> launcher: subscribe - launcher --> pipeline: run - bigquery -> prep: query - features -> prep: fetch features - prep -> train -> evaluate - evaluate -> models: register - models -> endpoint: deploy - endpoint -> monitor: request logs # The retraining loop climbs back to the triggers; written in layout order with the # arrowhead at the start so Cloud Logging stays a publisher beside Cloud Scheduler. - { from: logging, to: monitor, arrow: start, line: dashed, label: drift alerts } - pipeline ..> artifacts, metadata

svg.title: MLOps on Google Cloud with Agent Platform
svg.desc: MLOps on Google Cloud with Agent Platform. 18 components in 5 groups. Connections: Data scientists to Source repository (push); Source repository to Cloud Build (build trigger); Cloud Build to Artifact Registry (push); Artifact Registry to Cloud Run functions (pipeline template); Cloud Scheduler to Pub/Sub (publish); Cloud Logging to Pub/Sub (publish); Pub/Sub to Cloud Run functions (subscribe); Cloud Run functions to Agent Platform Pipelines (run); BigQuery to Validate and transform (query); Feature Store to Validate and transform (fetch features); Validate and transform to Managed Training; Managed Training to Evaluate and validate; Evaluate and validate to Model Registry (register); Model Registry to Endpoint (deploy); Endpoint to Model Monitoring (request logs); Cloud Logging to Model Monitoring (drift alerts); Agent Platform Pipelines to Cloud Storage; Agent Platform Pipelines to Vertex ML Metadata.

text.tspan: MLOPS ON GOOGLE CLOUD WITH AGENT PLATFORM
Cloud Build ships the pipeline; Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI) trains, registers and serves the model, and drift alerts
